kind: feasibility pilot (1 problem), a blueprint's holes to the Kaggle prover; no claim
supersedes: pilot-guided-2026-11-15 (run 43776896439): arm B closed holes 5 and 6 by Lean's recipes; arm C 8 asked, 0 answered, every ask refused HTTP 503 provider_busy while the ladder (run 43773519397) held requesty-leanstral-1-5. Inconclusive by its own rule. Three router pilots, three starved on lanes shared with the ladder
question: do samples from a Lean-trained prover (Goedel-Prover-V2-8B) come back as complete Lean proofs of this blueprint's holes, and do any close a hole Lean's recipes leave open? Nothing else is read from this run

blueprint.note: the only gated blueprint for this problem; the export refuses if the blueprint or the target on disk is not these hashes (blueprint.kaggle_work), every answer carries them, and judge_guided judges nothing if either differs at judge time

export: all 6 holes, each its own file with the earlier statements as hypotheses bp_1.. (blueprint.kaggle_work); 48 samples planned, in hole order, the kernel's chunks of 2 holes; holes Lean closes at judge time (5 and 6 in run 43776896439) are sampled too and those samples count as generated and unread

generation.model: Goedel-LM/Goedel-Prover-V2-8B, no revision pinned (the kernel downloads the current one; each answer's config records the model name only)
generation.settings: max_tokens 16000, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, half precision, 2 x T4 (tools/prover_kernel.py at the commit that carries this manifest)
generation.prompt: the kernel's PROMPT, unchanged: the hole's file with `sorry`, then the proof-plan instruction
generation.expected: about 160 s a sample by the last batches' rate, so about 2.1 h of the week's 30 free GPU hours plus the model load; $0

judging.lean: leanprover/lean4:v4.33.1, mathlib v4.33.1 (lake-manifest.json), the judge of tools/check.py
judging.order: Lean's 30 baseline recipes on every hole first (replay.baseline_one); then each sample of an open hole in sample order; a sample must contain a fenced block with `theorem sb_goal` (prover.final_proof), else it is read with no proof; a rejected proof goes through the free chain (toolscore.hole_repair) before it counts; the first accept closes the hole
judging.attribution: closed_by is lean or kaggle-goedel-prover-v2-8b; a try the free chain rescued carries repaired=true and is reported as prover plus chain, never prover alone

endpoint: from the row in ledger/stall/guided-<id>-<stamp>.jsonl: per hole planned and generated samples; samples read with a complete proof, read without, unread; holes closed by Lean, by a raw sample, by a repaired sample, failed, unattempted, judge_unfinished; whole proof accept, reject (with its reason) or NOT CHECKED when final is null
incomplete_if: truncated is true (a hole got fewer samples than planned: the kernel stops at its GPU budget and still ends as complete)
judging_complete is false (a sample or the whole proof hit Lean's timeout or memory limit)
no answers came back, or the blueprint or target changed since export
an_incomplete_run: is recorded as incomplete and is not pushed again on its own; a new manifest is a person's call
isolation: the Kaggle GPU kernel is this repo's own and shares no router lane with the ladder; the GPU leg pushes this batch before any other kind
credit: a solve here is guided: the guide chose the propositions, Lean and the prover (plus the free chain) proved every step; never 'free models plus tools'. Measurement rows committed; the accepted TEXT is held in the prover run's artifact (SB_GUIDED_OUT, 30 days), not in verified/, ledger/ or on the site, until the lab decides how guided solves are shown
claim: none. One problem, one blueprint, 8 samples a hole: a yes or no on whether this route produces usable hole proofs, not a rate and not tool lift
before_any_comparative_claim: REQUIRED: a matched control (the same prover, the same sample budget, cold on the whole problem in the same batch) and more than one problem; until then this is feasibility evidence only
not_verified_before_this_run: the artifact step in prover.yml and the kernel with `guided` entries have only been exercised in unit tests
known_gap: a batch that returns an empty answers file stops the workflow before judging (prover.yml), so no row is written for it; no further push follows, and the gap is read from the run, not the ledger (Codex 20261116T001213948778Z f5)
